blocks.text: 14. Compatibility Route C-17, the Ghost Line

Real-world analogue: An aging railway switchyard, old telephone exchange, utility corridor, public-records basement, legacy computer room, and accessibility route kept alive because people still depend on it.
World relation: Open World public service and Pilgrim World connective function. Continuity appears through obligations and dependencies that modernization plans fail to see.
Connection to newer locations: C-17 connects to the Underway of Returning Signals, Pale Concordance Station, Urban Canyon Hive, City of Rainward Roofs, and Valley That Restores Wrong.

Abstract or metaphorical relation: “Obsolete” often means that the institution has stopped seeing the people a system still serves. Maintenance becomes recognition when both sides begin adapting to the other’s presence.
